Subject: Request: quick fleet availability + temporary reserve for EmberAI late-stage

Ben/Marissa —

Heads-up: EmberAI (EMB-2026-042) asked for a firm start date for a dedicated pool if we move forward. They are late-stage (quietly asking for a Q4 ramp), and PM/Procurement are requesting a 2-week temporary hold while they finalize the contract language. They want to lock ~32 A100-equivalent slots initially, with possible burst to 64 during POC.

Can someone run a quick availability check for the US clusters (NVMe-backed racks) and tell me:
- how many A100-equivalent slots we can hold right now without impacting committed Dedicated customers
- any restrictions/lead time on creating a soft reserve (how we surface this in the capacity planner)
- ETA to put a short-term hold that can be released automatically if no deal signature in 21 days

I attached the Ember capacity request and a one-pager on the expected usage pattern (short tokens but high concurrency) — they are particular about latency.

I also want us to be conservative: don't promise more capacity than we can isolate without violating other customers' SLOs. If we need to stitch together equivalent GPUs (mix of A100s and A30s with quantization), call that out.

Thanks — this is time-sensitive; they want confirmation before the legal team sends redlines today.

--
Mina Haddad

Mina —

Quick scan attached: gpu_inventory_snapshot_20260816.csv. TL;DR:
- US-region NVMe racks: 48 A100-equivalent slots free today (after respecting existing Dedicated commitments).
- If we need exact A100 80GB SKUs only: 28 pure matches available.
- Mixed-fleet (A100 + A30) equivalent to 32 A100-e slots can be provisioned immediately but would require a quantization/profile guidance doc for Ember to avoid perf regressions.

Soft-reserve mechanics:
- We can create a 21-day soft hold that blocks allocation in the autoscaler but does not consume billing capacity. This is a standard temporary reservation; ops needs an explicit ticket to ensure the hold is flagged for automatic release.
- If legal requests an SLA/escape clause, mark the reserve as "commit conditional" and add a manual approval step to extend beyond 21 days.

Risks/notes:
- We currently have a scheduled maintenance window next month on two NVMe racks (affects ~8 slots) — if that slips into the POC window we should pre-announce.
- If they plan high-concurrency (100+ concurrent user sessions), the prefix/KV cache will matter more than raw GPU count; we should propose KV cache sizing during the POC call.

I'll open the ops ticket now with the requested hold parameters.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Capacity & Supply Planning, Redwood Inference

Thanks — good data. Mina: I support a 21-day temporary reserve for EMB-2026-042 with the following guardrails:
- Reserve size: 32 A100-equivalent (allowing burst to 64 if they sign)
- Soft-reserve flag: "sales_pending_signature" so ops/allocations can easily identify
- Auto-release at 21 days unless I (or CS lead) manually extend after review
- If legal insists on an SLA-level commit prior to signature, we should route to dedicated-sales-review; don't sign anything that creates an immediate committed allocation without procurement approval.

I'll loop John in if we need to convert to a paid short-term commit. For now, Ben please proceed to open the ops ticket and mark the reserved slots.
